SECTION 5. Said tax shall be due and payable on and between the first day and thirtyfirst day of August, A.D. 2026 and all taxes remaining unpaid on the thirty-first day of August, A.D. 2026 shall bear interest from and after said first day of August A.D. 2026 and until collected, at the rate of twelve (12) per cent per annum, and all taxes and interest in addition to taxes shall be paid to the Town Treasurer immediately after the receipt thereof. Said tax may be paid in installments, the first installment of twenty-five (25) per centum on or before the thirtyfirst day of August, A.D. 2026 and the remaining installments as follows: twenty-five (25) per centum on or before the thirtieth day of November, A.D. 2026; twenty-five (25) per centum on or before the twenty-eight day of February, A.D. 2027 and twenty-five (25) per centum on or before the thirty-first day of May, A.D. 2027. If the first installment, or any succeeding installment of taxes is not paid by the last day of the respective installment period or periods as they occur, then the whole tax or remaining unpaid balance of the tax as the case may be, shall immediately become due and payable and shall carry until collected a penalty at the rate of twelve (12) per centum per annum from and after the first day of August, A.D. 2026 and until collected. Members of the armed forces and merchant marines of the United States in active service shall be exempt during the period of such service from the interest penalty requirements of this ordinance. SECTION 6. The taxpayers of the Town of North Providence have an option whereby one-tenth (1/10) of said tax will be due and may be payable each month commencing the first day of September, A.D. two thousand twenty-six and ending the thirtieth day of June, A.D. two thousand twenty-seven and shall bear the same interest as specified in Section 5 of this ordinance. Town Council members will attend for informational purposes only. No Town Council business will be discussed, deliberated, or acted upon 1. Call to Order 2. Roll Call 3. Approval of Minutes for October 7th Meeting Discussion/ Action 4. Request for a Waiver of Formal Development Plan Review for Business License Discussion/ Action 22 Moosup Valley Rd (A.P 02 Lot 38) Applicant David Johnston is requesting a waiver from the requirements of a Formal Development Plan Review for a property located at 22 Moosup Valley Rd., Foster, RI 02825 (A.P 02 Lot 38). Zoned Agricultural/ Residential (AR), the property contains a 900 sq. ft. dwelling, which is primarily used as a secondary home to the applicant and their family. In order to cover the home’s maintenance and carrying costs, the applicant would like to list the home for rental via Airbnb, between the months of June and September. Per sec. 38-191 of the Foster Code of Ordinance, short-term rentals and bed & breakfasts are considered an allowed use subject to Formal Development Plan Review in the AR, GB, and HC2 zoning districts. Per RIGL §45-23-50(b) a waiver of development plan review may only be granted upon finding the use will not “affect existing drainage, circulation, relationship of buildings to each other, landscaping, buffering, lighting, and other considerations of development plan approval, and that the existing facilities do not require upgraded or additional site improvements.” 5. Presentation of Final Draft Zoning Amendments by Planning Advisor Peter Lapolla Discussion Peter Lapolla will present to the Planning Board the final draft amendments to the Zoning Chapter of Foster’s Code of Ordinances. These amendments will require a formal vote by the Board before being transferred to the Town Council for final approval. Members of both the Town Council and Zoning Board of Review are invited to take part in this discussion. 6. Adjournment

The public is welcome to participate in Town Council meetings in several ways: • Citizens are invited to speak on the topic of a Public Hearing, which will be listed on the agenda. • Citizens may speak during Open Forum to clarify or comment on an item on the agenda or address items not on the agenda. o A Citizen may schedule a Request to Address with the Town Council no less than seven days before the meeting in which they would like to appear. text: POSTED – OCTOBER 28, 2026 REGULAR MEETING NOVEMBER 2, 2026 TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND The following items of business, having been filed with the Town Clerk under the Rules of the Council, will come before the Council at a regular meeting to be held on Monday, November 2, 2026 at 6:00 P.M. Executive Session and 6:30 P.M. Regular Meeting at the Middletown Town Hall, 350 East Main Road, Middletown, Rhode Island. Said meeting will be conducted in person. Virtual access will also be provided by telephone conference call/ webinar and members of the public may access and listen to the meeting in real-time by calling 1-877-8535257 (Toll Free) or 1-888-475-4499 (Toll Free) and entering Meeting ID: 835 6442 7347 or on the web at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83564427347; however, virtual access is being provided only as a convenience and is not an official "location" where access to the meeting is guaranteed. Being physically present at the meeting is the only way to guarantee complete access to the meeting, as the meeting will not be paused or rescheduled if the virtual access fails. If you choose to join the meeting by zoom or telephone, Council Rules allow for the Public to speak only during the Public Forum and Public Hearings. If calling in by telephone, pressing *9 raises your hand and pressing *6 will unmute. The items listed on the Consent portion of the agenda are to be considered routine by the Town Council and will ordinarily be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member of the Council, or a member of the public so requests and the Town Council President permits, in which event the item will be removed from Consent Agenda consideration and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. All items on this agenda, with the exception of the Public Forum Session, may be considered, discussed, and voted upon in executive session and/or open session. Pursuant to RIGL §42-46-6(b). Notice – “Nothing contained herein shall prevent a public body, other than a school committee, from adding additional items to the agenda by majority vote of the members. Such additional items shall be for informational purposes only and may not be voted on except where necessary to address an unexpected occurrence that requires immediate action to protect the public or to refer the matter to an appropriate committee or to another body or official.” Any person not a member of the Council, desiring to address the Council concerning a matter on the docket of the Council, not the subject of a Public Hearing, shall submit a written request to the Town Clerk stating the matter upon which he desires to speak. Persons are permitted to address the Council for a period not to exceed five (5) minutes. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG RECONSIDERATION The Middletown Town Council follows the codification of present-day general parliamentary law as articulated in Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised 10th edition (2000), together with whatever rules of order the Council has adopted for its own governance. The motion to reconsider is one of the motions that can bring a question again before an assembly, and is designed to bring back for further consideration a motion which has already been voted on: If, in the same session that a motion has been voted on, but no later than the same day or the next day on which a business meeting is held, new information or a changed situation makes it appear that a different result might reflect the true will of the assembly, a member who voted with the prevailing side can, by moving to Reconsider [RONR (10th ed.), p. 304-321] the vote, propose that the question shall come before the assembly again as if it had not previously been considered. (From Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised In Brief, Robert, Evans et al., De Capo Press, 2004) EXECUTIVE SESSION – 6:00 P.M. 1. Executive Session - Pursuant to provisions of RIGL, Sections 42-46-2, 42-46-4 and 4246-5 (a), (2) Collective Bargaining (FOP) and (2) Litigation (Opioid Litigation), (2) Potential Litigation and (5) Land Acquisition (351 East Main Road). Russel Jackson, for a Minor Subdivision with Unified Development Review to a single lot consisting of 40m083 sf of land area into two separate lots; Proposed Lot 1 will include a land area of 8,500 sf and will contain existing single family structure. Proposed Lot 2 will include 31,583 sf and the Episcopal Church, the Guild Hall, and a 3 family structure. The Applicant is requesting variances from the following sections of the City of Newport Zoning Ordinance in the R-10 Zone: Section 17.20.030 Dimension Requirements-Minimum Lot Area, to allow Proposed Lot 1 to be 8,500 square feet of land area where 10,000 is required. Section 17.20.040 Setback Requirements: Proposed Lot 1, to allow the existing building to be 11.88 feet from the Washington Street front property line, where 15 Page 1 of 18 Monday October 5, 2026 Meeting Minutes Newport Planning Board Council Chambers Newport City Hall 43 Broadway feet is required, and 7.2 feet from the north side setback where 10 feet is required. Section 17.20.040 Setback Requirements: Proposed Lot 2, to allow the existing buildings to be 0.49 feet from the Poplar Street front property line and 4.2 feet from the Willow Street front property line, where 15 feet is required, and 0.71 feet from the east side setback where 10 feet is required. Section 17.20.050 Lot Coverage Requirements: to allow 22% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 1 and 40% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 2 where 20% is allowed. Section 17.104.020 Parking Space Standards: to allow Proposed Lot 2 to have 0 parking spaces where 111 are required. Secretary Pimental served as Acting Chair. The application was presented by J. Russell Jackson Esq. of Miller, Scott, Holbrook and Jackson on behalf of the applicant. Attorney Jackson introduced a compilation plan, prepared by Principe surveying, to show the size of the parcels within a 200 ft radius of the subject lot. The compilation plan was accepted by the Board, and is labeled as Exhibit A. Attorney Jackson provided an overview of the application contents and process, highlighting why the application originally proposed a 10,000 sf lot, but later resubmitted with a proposed 8,500 sf lot, which is undersized for the R-10 zoning district. Attorney Jackson first called Cheryl Lynne Abney, Senior Church Warden to provide insight on the Church’s programming, day-to-day operations, and future goals – including their reasons for pursuing a subdivision that proposes an undersized lot. Attorney Jackson then called Doug Mclean, and requested the Board recognize his title as a Planning and Zoning Expert, which they obliged. Mr. Mclean provided a high-level overview of his report, and his analysis of the requested variances, emphasizing neighborhood compatibility and consistency with the Comprehensive Plan. Board Member Greichen asked Mr. Mclean to elaborate on his recommendation to grant the variance regarding Proposed Lot 1’s northside setback (requesting 7.2’ where 10’ is required.) Mr Mclean emphasized the proposed lot line’s placement, which was designed to maintain pedestrian access to the church campus and argued that he believed it was due to a unique condition of the subject site. Board Member Huntsberry asked if there would be a change to the utility usage should the proposed subdivision be granted. The application team was unsure. Board Member Huntsberry requested confirmation on whether additional utilities would be required to be added in should the proposed subdivision be granted. Board Member Michaud asked for clarification on where outdoor programming takes place on the existing church campus. Mr. Mclean provided clarification that gatherings are typically held on areas labeled “lawn” on the site plan. Board Members Huntsberry and Michaud asked about the Historic District Commission’s purview on the property as a whole, as it is within the local historic district. However, Attorney Jackson reaffirmed there is no additional development being proposed through the proposed subdivision. Should there be changes to a structure, or landscape that is deemed historically significant, Historic District Commission approval would be sought. During public comment period, Direct Abutter Betty Cares of 31 Willow Street spoke against the application, stating the changes inflicted by the granting of the requested subdivision would be tremendous, and impractical as well as inharmonious with the neighborhood. Ms. Cares stated concern about immediate and long term impacts of the subdivision, specifically about continued development on the proposed subdivided lot and included existing tensions between the Church and the Cares Page 2 of 18 Monday October 5, 2026 Meeting Minutes Newport Planning Board Council Chambers Newport City Hall 43 Broadway family. Betty Cares submitted an impact statement, which was accepted by the Board and labeled as Exhibit B. Attorney Jackson made a closing statement, reinforcing arguments made during both witness testimonies. The Public Comment Period was closed. The Board unanimously voted to accept the Staff Report’s Findings of Fact, as amended. The Board proceeded to evaluate the variance requests. Their comments and discussion regarding each variance request are listed below: • 17.104.030– Minimum Lot Area. To allow Proposed Lot 1 to be 8,500 square feet of land area where 10,000 square feet is required. Secretary Pimental stated the presentations by the Church which articulated their programming and required space to achieve such programming, as well as the testimony indicating the proposed 8,500 sf lot, while smaller than the minimum requirement for the R-10 district, was still comptabile to the scale of lots within 200 sf indicated that this variance was sought due to a unique characteristic of both the structure, and land. Board Member Michaud concurred that the lot size was adequate based on the surrounding lots, and was satisfied that future development would be reviewed by the Historic District Commission. Board Member Greichen agreed and stated his observation of the existing sidewalk and pedestrian circulation through the Church campus, which is proposed to be located on the Proposed Lot 2 with the church buildings, supports the argument that this variance is sought due to unique characteristics of the land. • 17.20.040 – Setback Requirements. To allow the existing building on Proposed Lot 1 to be 11.88 feet from the Washington Street front property line where 15 feet is required, and 7.2 feet from the northside setback where 10 feet is required. Secretary Pimental observed that the siting of the historic building on Proposed Lot 1, specifically in relation to Washington Street, is a fixed circumstance that would only be remedied by a full demolition, and therefore the variance is sought due to a unique characteristic of the historic structure and land. • 17.20.040 – Setback Requirements. To allow the existing building on Proposed Lot 2 to be .49 feet from the Poplar Street front property line, 4.2 feet from the Willow street front property line where 15 feet is required; and, .71 feet from the east side setback where 10 feet is required. Board members again observed that the applicant cannot simply move the house, and therefore the variance is sought due to a unique characteristic of the historic structure and land. • 17.20.050 – Lot Coverage Requirements. To allow 22% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 1 where 20% is allowed. Board members acknowledged that a smaller lot with an existing building would most likely result in the need for a lot coverage variance. There is no new development proposed as part of this application. As Board Members already acknowledged that the variance requested pursuant to minimum lot area was due to a unique characteristic of the historic structure, and land, they felt the standards for this variance were met for the same reasons. • 17.20.050 – Lot Coverage Requirements. To allow 40% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 2 where 20% is allowed. Board members acknowledged that regardless of approval for the requested subdivision, Page 3 of 18 Monday October 5, 2026 Meeting Minutes Newport Planning Board Council Chambers Newport City Hall 43 Broadway the existing site conditions exceed the 20% lot coverage, due to the unique, historic character of the structures and land. • 17.104.020 – Parking Space Standards. To allow Proposed Lot 2 to have 0 parking spaces where 111 are required. Board members pointed out there is no change of use included in Proposed Lot 2. The 0 parking spaces are a unique characteristic of the historic site. Board Member Antonelli expressed concern regarding the potential parking need for new owners of the Proposed Lot 1 property, as it is not currently inhabited. Attorney Jackson clarified that Proposed Lot 1 has sufficient space for the installation of on-site parking, should the future owners need it. Board Member Greichen requested clarification on the existing parking needs, and if any site users have reserved parking spaces in the adjacent Willow Street Lot owned by the Church. Staff reiterated the applicant team’s testimony that the structure located at 59 Washington Street has been historically used as a rectory, which included a reserved spot in the Willow Street Lot. Regarding Proposed Lot 1, Director Reynolds noted that should a future curb cut application be granted, it may eliminate a street parking space. Attorney Jackson stated this would be the same process for any driveway on Poplar Street. Board Member Michaud requested clarification on the curb cut application process, which Director Reynolds stated as an application made through the Engineering Department. Board Members discussed the potential of imposing a condition requiring the applicant receive approval for a curb cut Proposed Lot 1 to allow for the installation of a driveway to serve the single-family home, prior to the granting of Final Approval for the proposed subdivision. Attorney Jackson pushed back on this condition, citing the delegation of final approval to the Engineering Department undermines the Subdivision Regulations, and is outside of the Board’s assigned purview. Board Members continued to discuss reservations about not imposing a condition related to Proposed Lot 1 lack of existing driveway. Director Reynolds reiterated that the applicant’s testimony stated there would be adequate room for the installation of a driveway on Proposed Lot 1 in the future. Secretary Pimental reiterated the findings that the granting of the requested variances would not alter the general character of the surrounding area, specifically citing the Compilation Plan submitted by the applicant (Exhibit A.) Board Member Michaud acknowledged the legislative intent of the R-10 Zoning Ordinance, but referencing Exhibit A and the Map of Nonconforming Properties in Newport According to Lot Size in the Newport Comprehensive Plan Housing Chapter said that the requested variances do not impair that intent. Board Members also noted that, should the proposed subdivision be granted, they did not believe Proposed Lot 1 could get subdivided further due to the siting of existing historic structure. Board Members agreed the granting of the requested dimensional variances would be minimal to the reasonable enjoyment of the site’s devoted use. Board Member Michaud motioned to approve the requested variances. Board Member Guzman Stokes seconded, and the motion was unanimously approved. The Public Hearing was closed. Leach, Chairwoman Heather Coia, Vice Chairwoman Mark Bushee, Treasurer Ryan Sylvestre, Member Peter Pare, Member Felicia Mahar, Member Raena Blumenthal, Member Smithfield Town Hall 64 Farnum Pike Smithfield, RI 02917 Katie Closson, Recording Secretary AGENDA NOVEMBER 4, 2026 7:00p.m. MEETING WILL BE HELD AT SMITHFIELD TOWN HALL, 2ND FLOOR CONFERENCE ROOM 64 FARNUM PIKE, SMITHFIELD, RI 02917 A) CALL TO ORDER B) EMERGENCY EVACUATION AND HEALTH NOTIFICATION C) APPROVAL OF THE CONSERVATION COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES - OCTOBER 7, 2026 D) OLD BUSINESS 1) Consider, discuss and act upon reports on meetings attended by Conservation Commission members. 2) Consider, discuss and act upon the maintenance of conservation areas including the Conservation Center. - Trail Subcommittee Report 3) Consider, discuss and act upon the following goals for 2026/2027. - Continue to remain visible within the community in terms of what the Conservation Commission does. -Facebook Page for Conservation Commission - Consider, discuss and act upon the following events: -Discuss Smithfield’s 300 Anniversary, Tercentenary, and Apple Trail Days - Assessing Water Quality Issues in Town: Goals, Strategies, Resources and Next Steps - RIDEM Forestry Division -Urban & Community Grant Program and Next Steps 4) Discuss and act upon Woonasquatucket River Watershed Council activities at the Conservation Center. 5) Consider, discuss and act upon informal and formal liaisons to other related Town boards and commissions. 6) Financial Review - Conservation Commission E) NEW BUSINESS 1) Consider, discuss and act upon approval of the payment of bills submitted to the Conservation Commission. 2) Consider, discuss and act upon approval of the 2027 Conservation Commission meeting schedule. 3) Consider, discuss and act upon approval of meeting time change. F) PUBLIC COMMENT G) ADJOURNMENT AGENDA POSTED: November 2, 2026 The public is welcome to any meeting of the Smithfield Conservation Commission. If communication assistance (readers/interpreters/captions) is needed or any other accommodations are needed to ensure equal participation, please contact the Smithfield Town Managers Office at 401-233-1010 at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the meeting.

title: Barrington Conservation Commission 2026-11-05 agenda (filed 2026-11-02 11:35 ET)
text: SPECIAL MEETING Barrington, Rhode Island BARRINGTON HOUSING AND ZONING COMMUNITY WORKSHOP NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN THAT A PUBLIC WORKSHOP WILL BE HELD ON: THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 05, 2026, AT 6:00 P.M.-7:30 P.M. COUNCIL CHAMBER, BARRINGTON TOWN HALL 283 COUNTY ROAD, BARRINGTON, RI The Town of Barrington is working with a team from Libra Planners to analyze our Zoning Ordinance to identify ways to support the creation of more high quality, affordable housing in Town. To ensure this analysis is responsive to Barrington’s needs, this second community workshop is being held to get more feedback from residents and stakeholders. This 90-minute workshop will provide key takeaways from meeting 1 and engagement in activities that will allow participants to learn about and discuss housing preferences with neighbors, Town officials, and the consultant team. All interested residents, business owners, and stakeholders are encouraged to attend. This notice is issued for the following Boards and Committees due to the potential for a quorum to be present: Town Council; Planning Board; Zoning Board; Housing Board of Trustees; Economic Development Committee; Technical Review Committee; Barrington Conservation Commission; Open Space Committee; Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee; Veteran’s Advisory Committee; Senior Services Advisory Board. No official action will be taken by these public bodies. Members of the listed Boards and Committees may participate in the noticed public workshop; however, their participation will be limited to discussion and information-gathering purposes. ALL QUESTIONS RELATING TO THIS CAN BE DIRECTED TO THE PLANNING ASSISTANT BETWEEN 9 a.m. AND 12:00 p.m OR AT GELLIOT@BARRINGTON.RI.GOV OR 401-247-1900 EXT. 326. ALL PLANNING BOARD MEETINGS ARE AUDIO-RECORDED. All town meetings are open to the public. The Town of Barrington will provide reasonable accommodations to ensure equal meeting participation. To request an accommodation to participate in a meeting, please submit your request by calling (401) 247-1900 Ext. 301 (Town Clerk’s office) or write a letter to the Town Clerk, Town of Barrington, 283 County Road, Barrington, RI 02806. Deaf and Hard of Hearing callers can dial 711 “Relay” or through a relay service provider to request an accommodation at the Town Clerk’s office. The Barrington Town Hall, Barrington Public Library, and Barrington Public Safety Building are accessible to people with disabilities. Agenda posted on November 2, 2026, at Barrington Town Hall and the Barrington Public Library and on Secretary of State Web Site.

Ordinance of the council of the City of East Providence ordering the assessment and collection of property tax on the ratable real estate and tangible personal property Member Aye Nay Fogarty Lawson Rego Sousa Rodericks 2. An ordinance authorizing the Director of Finance to borrow funds in anticipation of taxes Member Aye Nay Fogarty Lawson Rego Sousa Rodericks XVII. POSTED: STATE OF RHODE ISLAND CITY OF EAST PROVIDENCE CHAPTER ORDINANCE OF THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EAST PROVIDENCE ORDERING THE ASSESSMENT AND COLLECTION OF PROPERTY TAX ON THE RATABLE REAL ESTATE AND TANGIBLE PERSONAL PROPERTY THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EAST PROVIDENCE HEREBY ORDAINS: SECTION L. Section 16-50 entitled “Assessment” of Article IV entitled “Property Tax on Ratable - Real Estate and Tangible Personal Property and Excise Tax on Registered Motor Vehicles and Trailers” of Chapter 16 of the Revised Ordinances of the City of East Providence, Rhode Island, 1998, as amended, entitled “Taxation.” is amended to read as follows: That the Council of the City of East Providence hereby orders the assessment and collection of a tax on ratable real estate and tangible personal property in a sum not more than One Hundred Twenty-Seven Million Two Hundred Five Thousand Three Hundred and Eight Two ($127,205,382) dollars. Said tax is for ordinary expenses, for the payment of interest and indebtedness, in whole or in part, of said city, and for other purposes authorized by law. The Tax Assessor shall assess and apportion said tax on the inhabitants and ratable property of said city as of the 31st day of December, 2026 at twelve o'clock Eastern Standard Time, according to law, and shall on completion of said assessment, date and sign same and shall make out and certify to the Tax Collector of the City of East Providence, who is charged with the duties for the collection of taxes, on or before the 15th day of June, 2027 a complete list of the names of the persons taxed and of the total value of all the real estate and tangible personal property assessed against each person, and also the total amount assessed against each person on said real estate and tangible personal property, opposite the name of the person or persons assessed. Upon receipt of the certified tax list by the Tax Collector, she shall proceed and collect said tax on the persons and estates liable thereof; said tax shall be due and payable on and between the Ist day of June 2027 , and the 1st day of July, 2027 and provided further that if said tangible personal property and/or real estate taxes are paid in full on or before the Ist day of July, 2027, a discount of one and one half per centum (1.5%) of the total taxes on said tangible personal property and real estate shall be granted, and all taxes remaining unpaid on the Ist day of July, 2027 shall carry until collected a penalty at the rate of twelve per centum (12%) per annum from the 1st day of June, 2027 upon said unpaid tax, however, said taxes may be paid in four installments; the first installment of twenty-five per centum (25%) on or before the 1% day of July, 2027, the second installment of twenty-five per centum (25%) on or before the Ist day of September, 2027, the third installment of twenty-five per centum (25%) on or before the Ist day of December, 2027 and the fourth installment of twenty-five per centum (25%) on or before the 1st day of March, 2028. Each installment of taxes if paid on or before the last day of each installment period successively in order shall be free from any charge of interest and shall include an additional 7 business day grace period after the last due date of each installment. If any succeeding installment of taxes is not paid by the last date of the respective unpaid balance period or periods as they occur and after the 7 business day grace period, then the whole tax or remaining unpaid balance of the taxes as the case may be shall immediately become due and payable and carry until collected a penalty at the rate of twelve per centum, (12%) per annum. If any payment of taxes is made by check or electronic fund transfer (EFT) and said check is returned unpaid or said EFT is rejected and the city is assessed a fee from its bank for said bounced check/rejected EFT, a fee in the amount of $25.00 for a bounced check and a fee in the amount of $15.00 for a rejected EFT shall be due and owing by said taxpayer and said payment amount shall be added to the bill due and owing by the taxpayer. SECTION Il. That any of said taxes not paid on or before the 1st day of March 2027 shall forthwith be collected by levy upon the sale of real estate upon which it is assessed and by that or other due process of law in case of assessment upon tangible personal property. SECTION III. This ordinance shall take effect upon its second passage and all ordinances and parts of ordinances inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed. Given first passage and referred to at 6:30 p.m. for a hearing and consideration of final passage and adopted Attest: City Clerk of the City of East Providence, Rhode Island STATE OF RHODE ISLAND CITY OF EAST PROVIDENCE CHAPTER AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE DIRECTOR OF FINANCE TO BORROW FUNDS IN ANTICIPATION OF TAXES THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EAST PROVIDENCE HEREBY ORDAINS: SECTION I. The Director of Finance is authorized to borrow during the fiscal year ending October 31, 2027 such sums of money in anticipation of the property taxes of the year as may be permitted by law for the purpose of meeting the current liabilities and expenses of the City and that the Director of Finance is authorized to issue the note or notes of the City therefore and to refund such note or notes and any tax anticipation notes of a prior year to the extent permitted by law. SECTION II. This ordinance shall take effect upon its second passage and all ordinances and parts of ordinances inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed. Given first passage and referred to at 6:30 p.m. for a hearing and consideration of final passage and adopted Attest: City Clerk of the City of East Providence, Rhode Island

PH-2 Chapter 32-ZONING, Article XXVIII.-Rural Business Zoning District, Sec. 32-166.-Permitted Uses. (2nd reading) All uses permitted within the rural business district shall require a special use permit, unless otherwise indicated. Those uses permitted within the rural business district by special use permit are: Veterinary hospital Specialty service businesses Trade school Appliance repair Landscaping services Wholesale business Light assembly Commercial agriculture Automotive repair Wholesale storage Manufacturing uses Greenhouse/Nursery Tele exchange/call center Restaurant (full-service only, drive-thru prohibited) Personal service businesses Catering Service Bank Office building Commercial recreation structure Boat repair and service Communication studio Plumbing, welding, carpentry Retail sales of goods produced onsite Funeral home/Mortuary Farm* Cannabis retailer Boat and Trailer Storage Accessory to Boat Repair, Service and Manufacturing Telecommunication antenna attached to existing structures and modifications thereto Wood-related retail and services (including stoves, parts and wood-based fuel) 8 *A farm that is greater than ten (10) acres and has been in operation as a farm engaged in agriculture, horticulture, stabling of animals, commercial greenhouses or nurseries, and aquaculture, engaged in any form of such listed activities ten years prior to seeking designation as a farm, shall be considered a farm for purposes of this ordinance and a permitted use, without need for a special use permit, in the Rural Business District.
